comparisons.peer_summary: Inventory is valued at standard cost adjusted for lower of cost or net realizable value using assumptions about future demand and market conditions, with excess or obsolescence reserves based on specific facts and circumstances such as technology changes or demand decreases.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies rely on assumptions about future demand to manage inventory risk, but AMD details the methodology for valuation adjustments while AVGO lists demand drivers. AMD values inventory using 'assumptions about future demand and market conditions' and considers 'other-than-temporary decreases in demand', which corresponds to AVGO's identification of 'anticipated or actual demand for AI-related products' and 'distributors' product inventory' as key demand factors.

sentences.text: • anticipated or actual demand for AI-related products;
• our distributors' product inventory and end customer demand;
We value inventory at standard cost, adjusted to approximate the lower of actual cost or estimated net realizable value using assumptions about future demand and market conditions.

In determining excess or obsolescence reserves for products, we consider assumptions such as changes in business and economic conditions, other-than-temporary decreases in demand for our products, and changes in technology or customer requirements.

comparisons.peer_topic: AI Product Market Success and Strategy Risks
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel faces significant risks related to the market success of its AI product offerings and the evolving demand landscape. The company has experienced limited market success with accelerators, recognizing $922 million in Gaudi AI inventory-related charges in 2024. The rapidly evolving and unpredictable AI market presents additional risks regarding shifts in customer spend toward GPUs, the potential insufficiency of investments in AI PCs and data center products, and hurdles regarding demand materialization, third-party software development, and competition from established rivals.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies identify the rapidly evolving and unpredictable nature of AI demand as a key factor affecting product demand, but INT reports limited market success and significant inventory write-downs for its AI offerings, whereas AVGO frames AI demand as a general driver without disclosing similar failure metrics. AVGO lists 'anticipated or actual demand for AI-related products' as a specific factor affecting demand, while INTC explicitly states that 'The markets and use cases for products with AI capabilities have been rapidly evolving, are difficult to predict, and may impact demand for our products' and notes it had 'limited market success with our accelerator offerings' resulting in '$922 million in Gaudi AI accelerator inventory-related charges'.

sentences.text: The demand for our products has been affected in the past, and is likely to continue to be affected in the future, by various factors, including the following:
• anticipated or actual demand for AI-related products;
On the product side, we have had limited market success with our accelerator offerings, and in 2024 we recognized $922 million in Gaudi AI accelerator inventory-related charges.
The markets and use cases for products with AI capabilities have been rapidly evolving, are difficult to predict, and may impact demand for our products.

comparisons.peer_summary: Intel operates in a highly competitive and rapidly changing industry, with intensified competition due to the proliferation of AI and high demand for AI-related products, including competition from ARM-based ecosystems and internally developed semiconductors by OEMs and cloud providers.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies acknowledge that the proliferation of AI has intensified their competitive environment and affected demand, but INTC focuses on the source of competition (other chipmakers and ecosystems) while AVGO focuses on the customer adoption rate. AVGO cites 'the rate at which our present and future customers and end-users adopt our products and technologies... including our AI related products' as a demand factor, while INTC states its 'competitive environment has intensified... including as a result of the proliferation of AI and high demand for AI-related products'.

sentences.text: • the rate at which our present and future customers and end-users adopt our products and technologies in our target markets, including our AI related products, and the rate at which our customers' products that include our technology are accepted in their markets;

Our competitive environment has intensified in recent years, and we expect it to continue to do so in the future, including as a result of the proliferation of AI and high demand for AI-related products and services.

comparisons.peer_summary: 2023 was characterized by weak demand in many end markets due to macroeconomic challenges and inventory reductions, leading to significant drops in average selling prices for DRAM and NAND, as well as revenue declines across all segments.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies cite macroeconomic conditions and customer inventory reductions as factors affecting demand, but MU reports a specific period of weak demand and price declines, whereas AVGO lists these as general ongoing factors. AVGO identifies 'customer loss, economic conditions... [and] our distributors' product inventory' as factors, while MU details that '2023 was a year of weak memory and storage industry demand... stemming from global macroeconomic challenges and customer actions to reduce inventory levels', which led to revenue declines.

sentences.text: The demand for our products has been affected in the past, and is likely to continue to be affected in the future, by various factors, including the following:
• our distributors' product inventory and end customer demand;
In contrast, 2023 was a year of weak memory and storage industry demand in many end markets, stemming from global macroeconomic challenges and customer actions to reduce inventory levels.

These conditions, which began in the fourth quarter of 2022 and persisted into early 2024, led to significant reductions in average selling prices for both DRAM and NAND and reductions in bit shipments for DRAM.

comparisons.peer_topic: Causes of Inventory Excess or Obsolescence
comparisons.peer_summary: Situations that may result in excess or obsolete inventory include changes in business/economic/market conditions, sudden demand decreases, technological obsolescence, new product introductions, demand estimation errors, long lead-time ordering, government regulations, or competitive actions. Cancellation or deferral of customer purchase orders could also result in holding excess inventory.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies identify sudden demand decreases and technological changes as risks to inventory levels, but NVDA provides a detailed list of operational causes for excess inventory while AVGO broadly links demand to 'distributors' product inventory'. NVDA lists 'changes in business and economic conditions... sudden and significant decreases in demand... [and] inventory obsolescence because of changing technology' as causes for excess inventory, aligning with AVGO's mention of 'distributors' product inventory' and 'economic conditions' affecting demand.

sentences.text: The demand for our products has been affected in the past, and is likely to continue to be affected in the future, by various factors, including the following:
• our distributors' product inventory and end customer demand;

Situations that may result in excess or obsolete inventory or excess product purchase commitments include changes in business and economic conditions, changes in market conditions, sudden and significant decreases in demand for our products, inventory obsolescence because of changing technology and customer requirements, new product introductions resulting in less demand for existing products or inconsistent spikes in demand, failure to estimate customer demand properly, ordering in advance of historical lead-times, government regulations and the impact of changes in future demand, or increase in demand for competitive products, including competitive actions.

comparisons.peer_topic: Inventory Commitments and Manufacturing Lead Times
comparisons.peer_summary: Inventory and capacity purchase commitments are based on customer demand forecasts. Manufacturing lead times can be long, sometimes exceeding twelve months, and the company may place non-cancellable orders in advance of historical lead times, paying premiums and deposits to secure supply. The company also adjusts to competitor actions and macroeconomic conditions.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies discuss the impact of customer demand forecasts and timing on their supply chain, though NVDA details long manufacturing lead times and pre-payment of commitments while AVGO highlights distributor inventory levels. NVDA states its 'inventory and capacity purchase commitments are based on forecasts of future customer demand' and notes that 'manufacturing lead times can be and have been long', whereas AVGO cites 'our distributors' product inventory' as a key factor affecting demand.

sentences.text: • our distributors' product inventory and end customer demand;
Our inventory and capacity purchase commitments are based on forecasts of future customer demand.
Our manufacturing lead times can be and have been long, and in some cases, extended beyond twelve months for some products.

comparisons.peer_summary: Inventory is measured at lower of cost or net realizable value, considering judgments on future demand and macroeconomic impacts; for fiscal 2024 and 2023, the net effect of estimate changes was less than 2% of cost of revenues.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies use assumptions about future demand and market conditions to manage inventory valuation, but QCOM quantifies the financial impact of estimate changes while AVGO discusses the factors influencing demand itself. QCOM measures inventory at lower of cost or net realizable value 'considering judgments and estimates related to future customer demand and other market conditions', which parallels AVGO's discussion of how 'anticipated or actual demand' and 'distributors' product inventory' affect the demand environment.

sentences.text: The demand for our products has been affected in the past, and is likely to continue to be affected in the future, by various factors, including the following:
• anticipated or actual demand for AI-related products;

We measure inventory at the lower of cost or net realizable value considering judgments and estimates related to future customer demand and other market conditions, such as the impact of the macroeconomic environment in fiscal 2023, which negatively impacted consumer demand for smartphones and other devices that incorporate our products and technologies.
